title: introduce-consent-forwarder-rbacv2-assertion-proxy-and-kms-envelope
author: Lina Ortega
release_notes: Add consent-forwarder service that validates operator claims, signs transient RBAC v2 assertions with KMS envelopes, and routes audit events to region-aware sinks. Includes RBAC templates and helms for private deployments.
body:
Summary: This PR adds a lightweight consent-forwarder service and an RBAC v2 assertion proxy that issues short-lived operator assertions sealed by the KMS envelope layer. The forwarder uses tenant consent flags to determine whether audit payloads can be forwarded to third-party compliance sinks and pins sinks by region when the tenant has region-restriction metadata. Motivation: customers with strict data residency and consent obligations asked for an auditable, operator-scoped forwarding path that preserves residency guarantees and provides cryptographic proof that a tenant consented to off-platform forwarding. Design highlights: 1) consent-forwarder service (golang) that validates the tenant record, attached consent flags, and the operator scope; 2) assertion-proxy that emits an RBAC v2 assertion token (signed envelope) using our KMS envelope primitives; 3) region pin resolution: forwarder consults tenant region_hint and cluster zone map to pick the proper sink; 4) audit envelope metadata is augmented with assertion_fingerprint, sealed_kms_key_id, and residency_tag to allow downstream verifiers to validate chain-of-consent without leaking tenant PII; 5) rollout strategy includes a shadow-mode where forwarding is logged but not sent, and a canary that enables forwarding for opt-in tenants only. Checklist:
- [x] Implement consent-forwarder service and API routes
- [x] Add RBAC v2 assertion templates and a template renderer for operator-scoped assertions
- [x] Integrate with KMS envelope primitives (seal/unseal) and include new envelope unit tests
- [x] Add region pinning logic with fallback to region-affinity policy
- [x] Document new configuration knobs in docs/rbac-v2/consent-proxy.md
- [x] Add helm template for private deployment and example values
- [x] Add integration tests validating end-to-end envelope verification
- [x] Add observability: tracing spans, token-level metric, and per-sink success/failure counters

Motivation/context: Related customer asks (Linear ENG-2031) and compliance review items (SEC-88). This PR is intentionally conservative on what is forwarded by default (shadow first) and requires explicit tenant consent to transition to active forwarding. Rolling back is straightforward: disable consent-forwarder module via feature flag and revoke assertion signing permission from the KMS role.

Security considerations: assertion tokens are short-lived (1 minute) and include a nonce/nonce-hash to protect against replay. The KMS envelope used to sign assertions is restricted to the assertion service principal; audit_forwarder has a distinct KMS role for encrypting envelopes destined for sinks. All forwarded audit payloads are hashed with a salt derived from a tenant-scoped key before leaving the cluster when configured for pseudonymization.

Operational notes: default deployment is sidecar-less as a cluster service. For Private installations we ship a helm chart and a configuration CRD that ties into the existing audit routing. The default retention and forwarding rate is controlled with two knobs: max_forward_rate_per_tenant and shadow_sample_ratio.

Files touched (high level): src/services/consent-forwarder/main.go, pkg/rbac/templates/operator-assertion.tmpl, pkg/kms/envelope.go, charts/redwood-private/templates/consent-forwarder.yaml, docs/rbac-v2/consent-proxy.md, tests/integration/consent_forwarder_test.py, .github/workflows/consent-forwarder-ci.yaml, pkg/observability/forwarder_metrics.go

Backwards compatibility: None of the existing RBAC decision flows are changed for normal request authorization; this adds an augmentation path for audit forwarding and a new signed assertion flow that is opt-in per tenant.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag off; 2) Deploy to staging and enable shadow mode; 3) Collect metrics for 7 days, iterate on telemetry; 4) Enable canary for 3 small tenants with manual consent; 5) Gradual enablement per region after compliance sign-off.

Follow-ups: 1) Add an admin UI to review forwarded audit entries (PM request); 2) Add tenant-level consent audits to the token indexer; 3) Run a red-team to validate replay and key compromise scenarios.
commits_summary: feat(consent-forwarder): add service and API routes; feat(rbac): add operator assertion templates; feat(kms): add envelope sign/verify helpers; test(integration): add consent-forwarder e2e tests; chore(helm): add chart for private deploy; fix(lint): address golangci-lint findings
review_conversation: Ravi Kaur: Can you explain how tenant consent is proved to a third-party sink? Lina Ortega: We attach a sealed assertion envelope (KMS key id reference + signature) and an assertion_fingerprint that downstream verifiers can validate using a published verification endpoint. We also include a residency_tag so sinks can enforce region restrictions. Jules Morgan: Please add a histogram for forward latency and a counter for KMS failures. Lina Ortega: Added forward_latency_histogram and kms_forward_failures counter in observability; updated tests to simulate KMS errors. Evelyn Park: LGTM after small nits. Ravi Kaur: Approved pending the documented threat model in docs/rbac-v2/consent-proxy.md. Lina Ortega: Added a threat model subsection and a short remediation checklist. CI: initial lint step failed (golangci-lint) due to unused variable in envelope.go; fixed in follow-up commit. All checks now pass.
